To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mRNA expression of SLC2 and SLC5A family genes is different in PTCs with and without BRAF mutation and that higher expression of SCL5A5 mRNA is correlated with less PTC recurrences.

SLC5A4 and SLC5A6 mRNA expressions were positively correlated with each other, and SLC5AS mRNA expression was positively correlated with SCL2A4 mRNA expression, but negatively correlated with SCL 2A1 and SCL2A3 mRNA expressions.
expression of SLC2 and SLC5 mRNA was negatively and positively correlated with 18F-FDG and 131I uptake in PTC, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of SLC2 family and SLC5A family genes in PTC and the association with 18F FDGPET/CT and 131I WBS.
the molecular basis of the role of SLC5S mRNA expression in PTC.
the molecular mechanism of FDG PET and WBS and provides a new perspective for PTC management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SLC5A family of genes is important in the pathogenesis and prognosis of PTC.
the expression of SLC2 and SLC5 mRNA is associated with the clinical outcome of PTC.
SLC5A mRNA is associated with PTC disease free survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SLC5A 5 expression may be a prognostic factor in PTC.
SLC5A4 and SLC2 mRNA expressions are associated with 131I and 18F-FDG uptake in PTC.
the expression of SLC2 and SLC5 mRNA may provide a molecular basis to understand the dynamics of 18F FDGE PET scans and 131I WBS in PTC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SLC5A mRNA expression can be used as a prognostic marker in PTC patients.
SLC5A4 and SLC2As are the most important factors in determining the prognosis of PTC.
SLC5A4 and SLC2 mRNA expression may be a better predictor for the prognosis of PTC patients with BRAF mutations.
